q: Which is the birth place of Ramanuja?
explanation: Ramanuja was born at Sriperumbudur in Tamil Nadu. Kaladi was Shankara's birthplace, Udupi Madhva's centre and Basava Kalyani Basavanna's.

notes.text: - Born at **Sriperumbudur** (Tamil Nadu); centre **Srirangam**; called **Ilaya Azhwar**; incarnation of **Adisesha / Lakshmana**.

q: Who was the Guru of Sankaracharya?
explanation: Adi Shankaracharya's guru was Govinda Bhagavatpada, himself a disciple of Gaudapada. Padmapada was Shankara's own disciple; Kumarila Bhatta was a Mimamsa scholar.

notes.text: - **Guru = Govinda Bhagavatpada** (disciple of Gaudapada); **Padmapada** was Shankara's own disciple.

q: Who was the founder of Advaita Philosophy?
explanation: Shankaracharya (8th c.) is the founder (chief exponent) of Advaita philosophy; Prabhakara Mishra was a Mimamsaka, Bhaskaracharya taught Bhedabheda, and Madhusudana Saraswati was a later Advaitin.

notes.text: - Born at **Kaladi, Kerala** (788); died 820; **founder of Advaita** philosophy (APPSC Endowment 2022) – not Bhaskaracharya, Prabhakara or Madhusudana Saraswati.

q: What was written by Adisankaracharya to praise the Goddess?
explanation: Saundarya Lahari, attributed to Adi Shankaracharya, is a hymn in praise of the Goddess (Tripurasundari); Sivananda Lahari and Bhujanga Stotram praise Shiva.

notes.text: - Wrote **Saundarya Lahari** in praise of the **Goddess**; Sivananda Lahari praises Shiva.

q: Who among the following was a contemporary of Purandara Dasa?
explanation: Purandara Dasa (1484-1564) lived in the reign of Sri Krishnadevaraya (1509-29); Saluva Narasimha and Veera Narasimha ruled earlier, and Akbar was in the north.

notes.text: - **Purandara Dasa** (1484-1564), Haridasa and "Pitamaha of Carnatic music", was a contemporary of **Sri Krishnadevaraya** (1509-29).

q: Kabir belonged to the tradition of
explanation: Kabir worshipped a formless God and belongs to the Nirguna Bhakti tradition; Tulsidas, Surdas and Mira represent Saguna Bhakti.

notes.text: - Born (tradition) to a **Brahmin widow**, raised by Muslim weavers **Niru and Nima**; disciple of **Ramananda**; **Nirguna Bhakti** (APPSC FRO).

q: In which holy place Ratha Yatra is celebrated as festival?
explanation: The Ratha Yatra (chariot festival) of Lord Jagannatha is celebrated at Puri, where Chaitanya spent his later years; Prayag and Haridwar host the Kumbha and Kumbhakonam the Mahamaham.

notes.text: - **Namdev** – **Varkari saint** (UPPCS 2004) – not Nimbarka, Chakradhara (Mahanubhava) or Ramdas (Samarth); tailor family; teacher **Visoba Khechar**; hymns in the Guru Granth Sahib; his nirguna bhakti **showed Islamic (Sufi) influence** (UP UDA 2010).

explanation: Mirabai belonged to the Rathore royal family of Merta, Rajasthan, and married into the Sisodia house of Mewar.

notes.text: - **Eknath** (1533-99) – Eknathi Bhagavata; **Tukaram** – abhangas; **Ramdas** – Dasbodh, guru of Shivaji.

explanation: Guru Nanak (born 1469 at Talwandi) founded Sikhism; Kabir and Eknath were Bhakti saints.

notes.text: - **Founder of Sikhism**; born **1469, Talwandi (Nankana Sahib)**, Khatri family; companion **Bhai Mardana**; **Guru ka Langar** (began at Kartarpur).

q: Which of the following written by Kancharla Gopanna?
explanation: Kancherla Gopanna (Bhakta Ramadasu) composed the Dasarathi Satakam while jailed in Golconda fort. Sumati Satakam is Baddena's, the tempting wrong option.

notes.text: - **Dasarathi Satakam = Gopanna** (APPSC G1 2002, asked three times) – NOT **Sumati Satakam** (Baddena), Bhaskara Satakam (Maravi Venkayya) or Vemana Satakam.
- Jailed **12 years in Golconda fort** by **Abul Hasan Tana Shah**; in prison he composed the **Dasarathi Satakam** (104 poems to Rama) and the Ramadasu kirtanas.

q: Naukacharitra is a musical treatise written by?
explanation: Nauka Charitram, a musical drama (opera), was written by Tyagaraja, who also wrote Prahlada Bhakti Vijayam. Annamacharya, Kshetrayya and Ramadasu did not write it.

notes.text: - **Nauka Charitram = Tyagaraja** (APPSC G1 1994), not Annamacharya, Kshetrayya or Ramadasu.

q: Who translated Dasarathi Satakam into English?
explanation: The APPSC key credits Dr. Bhanumathi Ramakrishna with the English translation of Kancherla Gopanna's Dasarathi Satakam; the singers Balamuralikrishna and S.P. Balasubrahmanyam were not its translators.

notes.text: - English translation of Dasarathi Satakam credited (APPSC G2 2001 key) to **Dr. Bhanumathi Ramakrishna**.

q: Which of the following is a work of Kancharla Gopanna?
explanation: Kancherla Gopanna (Bhakta Ramadasu) composed the Dasarathi Satakam while jailed in Golconda fort. Sumati Satakam is Baddena's, the tempting wrong option.

notes.text: - **Dasarathi Satakam = Gopanna** (APPSC G1 2002, asked three times) – NOT **Sumati Satakam** (Baddena), Bhaskara Satakam (Maravi Venkayya) or Vemana Satakam.
- Jailed **12 years in Golconda fort** by **Abul Hasan Tana Shah**; in prison he composed the **Dasarathi Satakam** (104 poems to Rama) and the Ramadasu kirtanas.

q: Which of the following has been authored by Kancherla Gopanna?
explanation: Kancherla Gopanna (Bhakta Ramadasu) composed the Dasarathi Satakam while jailed in Golconda fort. Sumati Satakam is Baddena's, the tempting wrong option.

notes.text: - **Dasarathi Satakam = Gopanna** (APPSC G1 2002, asked three times) – NOT **Sumati Satakam** (Baddena), Bhaskara Satakam (Maravi Venkayya) or Vemana Satakam.
- Jailed **12 years in Golconda fort** by **Abul Hasan Tana Shah**; in prison he composed the **Dasarathi Satakam** (104 poems to Rama) and the Ramadasu kirtanas.

q: Who is the singer and author of works known as Pancharatna Krutulu?
explanation: The Pancharatna kritis ('five gems') are Tyagaraja's most famous compositions, in Ghana ragas. Annamacharya, Kshetrayya and Ramadasu wrote sankirtanas, padams and kirtanas.

q: Who is the foremost composer of Carnatic music?
explanation: Tyagaraja (1767–1847), the greatest of the Carnatic Trinity, is regarded as the foremost composer of Carnatic music. Annamacharya was an earlier pioneer, not the foremost composer.

notes.text: - **Foremost composer of Carnatic music = Tyagaraja** (APPSC G2 2019); **pioneer of the kriti / sankirtana form = Annamacharya** (APPSC G2) – the same four options, two different stems.

q: Identify the odd man out:
explanation: Maharajapuram Viswanatha Iyer, Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer and Musiri Subramania Iyer were Carnatic vocalists. T.R. Mahalingam was a flautist, so he is the odd one out.

q: Renowned keerthanakara in Telugu
explanation: Thyagaraja (1767-1847) composed his kirtanas mainly in Telugu; Vijayadasa composed in Kannada and the Alvars in Tamil.

q: Who was the contemporary ruler of Vaggeyakara Annamacharya?
explanation: Tallapaka Annamacharya (1408–1503) was a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha Raya of Vijayanagara. Harihara, Deva Raya I and Deva Raya III ruled earlier.

notes.text: - Contemporary of **Saluva Narasimha Raya** (APPSC G2 2011) – not Harihara, Deva Raya I or III; also a contemporary of **Purandara Dasa**.

q: Who was the pioneer composer of the kriti form of Carnatic music?
explanation: Annamacharya, the earliest composer of sankirtanas, is regarded as the pioneer of the kriti form; Tyagaraja came three centuries later and perfected it.

notes.text: - Titles: **Pada Kavita Pitamaha**, Sankirtanacharya; earliest composer of sankirtanas → **pioneer of the kriti form**; the kirtana structure shaped later Carnatic music. Opposed untouchability (**Brahmam Okkate**).
- **Foremost composer of Carnatic music = Tyagaraja** (APPSC G2 2019); **pioneer of the kriti / sankirtana form = Annamacharya** (APPSC G2) – the same four options, two different stems.

q: Who was the composer of " Subhadra Kalyanam "?
explanation: Subhadra Kalyanam was composed by Tallapaka Timmakka (Tirumalamma), Annamacharya's wife and the first woman poet in Telugu. Molla wrote the Ramayanam.

notes.text: - **Subhadra Kalyanam / Parinayam = Tallapaka Timmakka** (APPSC G2; G2 2012) – not Molla, Rangajamma, Madhuravani or Gangadevi.

q: "Paramayogi Vilasamu" was authored by?
explanation: Paramayogi Vilasamu was written by Tallapaka Tiruvengalanatha (Chinnanna), Annamacharya's grandson, who also wrote Annamacharya Charitra and Usha Kalyanam.

notes.text: - **Paramayogi Vilasamu = Tallapaka Tiruvengalanatha** (APPSC Degree Lecturers 2011) – not Annamayya himself, Dhurjati or Ramaraja Bhushana.

q: Who is the author of Subhadra Parinayam?
explanation: Subhadra Parinayam (Subhadra Kalyanam) was written by Tallapaka Timmakka; Rangajamma wrote Mannarudasa Vilasam and Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam.

notes.text: - **Subhadra Kalyanam / Parinayam = Tallapaka Timmakka** (APPSC G2; G2 2012) – not Molla, Rangajamma, Madhuravani or Gangadevi.

q: After reorganization which of the following places is not in Andhra Pradesh?
explanation: The Akka Mahadevi caves lie across the Krishna from Srisailam, in Nagarkurnool district of Telangana, so after bifurcation they are not in Andhra Pradesh. Vedadri (NTR dt.), Nagarjunakonda (Palnadu dt.) and Mantralayam (Kurnool dt.) are in AP.

q: Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple is dedicated to:
explanation: The Mallikarjuna Swamy temple at Srisailam, one of the 12 jyotirlingas, is dedicated to Lord Shiva (with Bhramaramba).

q: The Pancharama Kshetras refers to?
options: Five Court Poets of Satakarni I
Five Court Poets of Satakarni II
Five ancient temples dedicated to Lord Shiva
Five ancient temples dedicated to Lord Vishnu
key_text: Five ancient temples dedicated to Lord Shiva
explanation: The Pancharama Kshetras are five ancient Shiva temples of Andhra: Amararama, Draksharama, Somarama, Ksheerarama and Kumararama. They have nothing to do with Satakarni's poets.

q: To which deity is the 'Kotappa Konda' temple dedicated?
explanation: Kotappakonda near Narasaraopet (Palnadu dt.) is a temple of Lord Shiva as Trikoteswara Swamy, famous for its Maha Shivaratri festival.

notes.text: - **Kotappakonda = Shiva temple** (AEE 2011; APPSC) – not Venkateswara, Vishnu or Krishna.

q: Vira Saivism was spread in Andhra by
explanation: Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya spread Virashaivism in Andhra in the Kakatiya age and founded Aradhya Saivism. Basava founded the movement in Karnataka, and Palkuriki Somanatha was its later Telugu poet.

notes.text: - **Virashaivism spread in Andhra by Panditaradhya** (APPSC G1 1983-84) – Basava founded it in Karnataka; Somanatha was its later Telugu poet.

q: Basava Purana was written by?
explanation: Palkuriki Somanatha wrote the Basava Puranam in Telugu dwipada, and also the Panditaradhya Charitra. Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya wrote Sivatattvasaram.

notes.text: - **Basava Purana = Palkuriki Somanatha** – not Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya (Sivatattvasaram).

q: Lingayats prayed to?
explanation: Lingayats (Virashaivas), followers of Basava, worship Lord Shiva in the form of the Ishtalinga worn on the body.

notes.text: - Lingayats worship **Shiva** in the form of the **Ishtalinga** worn on the body; theology **Shakti Vishishtadvaita**; **Kayaka** = honest labour, **Dasoha** = sharing.

q: Who wrote Veerabhadra Vijayam?
explanation: Veerabhadra Vijayam was Bammera Potana's first work, written at the request of his guru Ivaturi Somanaradhya; it is not by Srinatha, Tikkana or Errapragada.

notes.text: - **Veerabhadra Vijayam = Potana** (APPSC G2 2011, asked three times) – not Srinatha, Tikkana or Errapragada.

q: Who wrote Veerabhadra Vijayam?
explanation: Veerabhadra Vijayam was Bammera Potana's first work, written at the request of his guru Ivaturi Somanaradhya; it is not by Srinatha, Tikkana or Errapragada.

notes.text: - **Veerabhadra Vijayam = Potana** (APPSC G2 2011, asked three times) – not Srinatha, Tikkana or Errapragada.

q: Who was the author of Virabhadra Vijayam?
explanation: Veerabhadra Vijayam was Bammera Potana's first work, written at the request of his guru Ivaturi Somanaradhya; it is not by Srinatha, Tikkana or Errapragada.

notes.text: - **Veerabhadra Vijayam = Potana** (APPSC G2 2011, asked three times) – not Srinatha, Tikkana or Errapragada.

q: According to some opinions, Vontimitta is the birthplace of?
explanation: Most accounts make Bammera (Jangaon dt.) Potana's birthplace, but one tradition places it at Vontimitta in Kadapa district.

notes.text: - Native of **Bammera** (Jangaon dt., Telangana); one tradition places him at **Vontimitta (Ontimitta), Kadapa** (APPSC MPDO 1997).

q: First Telugu poetess who wrote Ramayana
explanation: Atukuri Molla (16th century, potter family of Gopavaram) was the first Telugu poetess to write the Ramayana (Molla Ramayanam). Timmakka wrote Subhadra Kalyanam.

notes.text: - **First Telugu poetess to write the Ramayana = Molla** (APPSC Geologist 2007).

q: ' Madhura Vijayam ' was composed by:
explanation: Madhura Vijayam (Veera Kamparaya Charitam), a Sanskrit poem, was written by Gangadevi, wife of the Sangama prince Kumara Kampana, on his conquest of Madurai.

notes.text: - **Madhura Vijayam = Gangadevi** – not Molla, Ramabhadramba or Madhuravani.

q: Identify the wrong match. (Author) (Literary Work)
explanation: Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam, not Marichi Parinayam, which is by Mohanangi, Krishnadevaraya's daughter. Molla–Ramayanam, Timmakka–Subhadra Kalyanam and Tirumalamba–Varadambika Parinayam are correct.

notes.text: - **Wrong match (APPSC G2): Gangadevi – Marichi Parinayam** (Marichi Parinayam is Mohanangi's); Molla – Ramayanam, Timmakka – Subhadra Kalyanam, Tirumalamba – Varadambika Parinayam are correct.

q: Point out from the following Sufis, who is from the Chishti Sufi Silsilah.
explanation: Saiyid Muhammad Gesudaraz of Gulbarga was a Chishti; Bahauddin Naqshband and Shah Waliullah were Naqshbandis and Bahauddin Zakariya a Suhrawardi.

notes.text: - **Not Chishti:** **Abdul Qadir Jilani** (Qadiri; RAS 2016); **Bahauddin Zakariya** (Suhrawardi; NDA 2017). **Chishti:** **Gesudaraz** (APPSC G1 2019) – not Bahauddin Naqshband, Bahauddin Zakariya or Shah Waliullah.

q: Which of the following Sufi saints was known as Garib Nawaz?
explanation: Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti of Ajmer is known as Garib Nawaz (benefactor of the poor).

notes.text: - **Garib Nawaz = Moinuddin Chishti** (APPSC G1 2017).

explanation: The dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, founder of the Chishti order in India, is at Ajmer.

q: The famous medieval Sufi saint, Gesudaraz, belonged to:
explanation: Saiyid Muhammad Gesudaraz (Banda Nawaz), the Chishti saint, belonged to Gulbarga, where his dargah stands.

q: In which city is the famous Urs of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti celebrated every year during the month of August?

explanation: The annual Urs of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti is held at his dargah in Ajmer; its date follows the Islamic month of Rajab, so it is not always in August.

notes.text: - Urs of Moinuddin Chishti = **Ajmer** (the date moves with the Islamic month Rajab).

q:
Which of the principles are common for Bhakti and Sufi movement ?

I. Monotheism

II. Asceticism

III. Religious tolerance

IV. Accepted the idol worship to some extent
explanation: Monotheism, asceticism and religious tolerance were common to both; idol worship was not accepted by the Sufis or by the nirguna Bhakti saints, so IV is wrong.

notes.text: - **APPSC G1 2023:** common principles = **I, II and III only** (monotheism, asceticism, tolerance); idol worship is the trap.

q: Hindustani music was largely influenced by:
explanation: Hindustani music was shaped largely by the Arabo-Persian music brought by Muslim rulers and Sufi musicians; European music had no such role.

q: In which city did the Prime Minister attend the 350th birth anniversary of Guru Gobind Singh in 2017?
explanation: PM Modi attended the 350th birth anniversary (Prakash Parv) celebrations of Guru Gobind Singh at Patna – his birthplace – on 5 January 2017 and released a stamp. Nanded is where the Guru died; Anandpur is where he founded the Khalsa.

notes.text: - **350th birth anniversary (Prakash Parv):** PM attended the celebrations at **Patna** (Gandhi Maidan) on **5 January 2017** and released a stamp – not Nanded, Amritsar or Anandpur.

q: Who was the tenth (10th) Guru of the Sikhs?
explanation: Guru Gobind Singh was the tenth and last Guru; he founded the Khalsa in 1699. Tegh Bahadur was the 9th, Har Kishan the 8th, and Banda Bahadur was his disciple, not a Guru.

notes.text: - **Guru Gobind Singh** (1666-1708) = **tenth and last human Guru** of the Sikhs – not Tegh Bahadur, Har Krishan or Banda Bahadur.

q: The word 'Sikh' means
explanation: 'Sikh' comes from the Sanskrit shishya – a disciple or learner of the Guru. 'Khalsa' means pure; soldier, monk and devotee are not the word's meaning.

notes.text: - **"Sikh"** = **disciple** (from Sanskrit **shishya**, learner) – not soldier, monk or devotee; **Khalsa** = "pure".

explanation: The Blue Water Policy, naval mastery of the Indian Ocean, was introduced by the first Viceroy Francisco de Almeida; Albuquerque turned to territorial conquest.

q: Which Fruit was introduced by the Portuguese to the Telugu soil?
explanation: The tomato, an American plant, came to the Telugu country with the Portuguese; banana, apple and orange were known in India long before.

notes.text: - **Bahadur Shah of Gujarat** was **killed by the Portuguese (1537)** – invited aboard a Portuguese ship during talks.

q: After coming to India, where did the Dutch establish their first factory in Andhra Pradesh?
explanation: The Dutch set up their first factory in Andhra (and India) at Masulipatnam in 1605, with Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah's permission; Nizampatnam (1606) and Pulicat (1610) came later.

q: What was the headquarters of the Dutch East India Company's establishments in India?
explanation: Nagapattinam (taken from the Portuguese in 1658) was the headquarters of the Dutch in India from 1690; before that the Coromandel HQ was Pulicat. Masulipatnam ('Musula') was their first factory.

notes.text: - **Headquarters:** **Pulicat** till **1689-90** = the Dutch capital / Governor's seat on the Coromandel and in Andhra; **Nagapattinam** after 1690 = HQ of Dutch settlements in India (APPSC G2 2005).

q: In which year did the Dutch establish their first factory at Pulicat, which was later abandoned?
explanation: The Dutch factory at Pulicat dates from 1610 (some books 1609), their second after Masulipatnam.

q: Where was the Governor of the Dutch Company based till 1689?
explanation: The Dutch Governor of the Coromandel was based at Pulicat till 1689-90, after which Nagapattinam became the HQ; Pondicherry was French and Madras English.

notes.text: - **Headquarters:** **Pulicat** till **1689-90** = the Dutch capital / Governor's seat on the Coromandel and in Andhra; **Nagapattinam** after 1690 = HQ of Dutch settlements in India (APPSC G2 2005).

q: At which place in Andhra did the Dutch East India Company set up its first factory?
explanation: The Dutch founded their first factory at Masulipatnam (Machilipatnam) in Andhra in 1605; Pulicat (1609-10), Surat (1616) and Bheemunipatnam (1641) came later.

notes.text: - **First Dutch factory:** **Machilipatnam 1605** (asked ×5: APPSC EO 2021, NDA 2010, ACF 2012, AP History PYQ); Pulicat came second.

q: Which of the following regions was a Dutch colony?
explanation: Bheemili (Bheemunipatnam, 1641) was Dutch. Yanam and Mahe were French, and Karaikal, briefly Dutch (1645), was French from 1739.

notes.text: - **Dutch colony among Yanam, Mahe, Karaikal, Bheemili:** **Bheemili** – Yanam and Mahe were French, and Karaikal (Dutch 1645) became French in 1739.
